Piedras Negras, Coahuila - The regional and municipal Civil Protection coordinations from the Central-Desert, Carboniferous, and Northern areas were summoned by the company Ferromex to participate in a training course on hazardous materials handling, which will take place at the railway company's facilities located on the borders of Nava and Piedras Negras, reported Francisco Contreras Obregón, the regional Civil Protection coordinator for Coahuila.

He noted that this training is of great importance, as the region has railway lines used for transporting hazardous materials through various municipalities, emphasizing the training provided by Ferromex through specialists.

During the course, Ferromex's training tank car and the Transcaer system will be utilized, tools that allow for the training of firefighting and emergency response teams, Contreras Obregón explained.

He added that some personnel from the Manantiales and Northern regions have already taken this course, making this training also a means to update their knowledge.

Through the border of Piedras Negras, hazardous materials such as ammonium nitrate, liquefied gas, and fuels, among other high-risk substances, are both imported and exported, which necessitates that firefighting and Civil Protection units are prepared to handle emergencies related to accidents involving the transportation of these products.

Contreras Obregón indicated that schools, universities, and private companies can also participate in these courses to train their students or personnel responsible for managing emergencies within their facilities.

New Nanoparticles Study Findings Have Been Reported by Investigators at Northwest University (N Modified Uniform Fe0 Nanoparticles Within Cnt for Efficient Removal of Methylene Blue From Wastewater)

2026 NOV 03-- By a News Reporter-Staff News Editor at Nanotech Daily-- A new study on Nanotechnology- Nanoparticles is now available. According to news originating from Shaanxi, People' s Republic of China, by NewsRx correspondents, research stated," Fe and N co-loaded carbon nanotubes were synthesized through a coordination-assisted strategy for methylene blue... 2026 NOV 03 (NewsRx) -- By a News Reporter-Staff News Editor at Nanotech Daily -- A new study on Nanotechnology - Nanoparticles is now available. According to news originating from Shaanxi, People's Republic of China, by NewsRx correspondents, research stated, "Fe and N co-loaded carbon nanotubes were synthesized through a coordination-assisted strategy for methylene blue MB removal. Structural characterization confirmed that Fe-N modification increased the defect density of CNT, improved pore accessibility, and promoted the dispersion of iron species."

Financial supporters for this research include National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC), State Key Laboratory of Clean and Efficient Coal Utilization, Taiyuan University of Technology.

Our news journalists obtained a quote from the research from Northwest University, "The ID/IG value increased from 1.08 for CNT to 1.10 for Fe-N/CNT, while the specific surface area of Fe-N/CNT reached 209.7 m2 g- 1. Under the optimized conditions, MB concentration of 100 mg L- 1, adsorbent dosage of 25 mg, and contact time of 120 min, Fe-N/CNT exhibited an adsorption capacity of 108.98 mg g-1. This value was much higher than those of pristine CNT (60.67 mg g-1) and Fe/CNT (41.43 mg g- 1). The adsorption behavior fitted well with the pseudo-secondorder kinetic model (R2 = 0.9998) and the Langmuir isotherm model (R2 = 0.9977). Mechanism analysis suggested that electrostatic attraction, hydrogen bonding, it-it stacking, pore filling, and Fe-Nx sites jointly contributed to MB adsorption. Fe-N/CNT retained 81% of its adsorption efficiency after five cycles and showed stable performance in cation-containing solutions, multi-dye systems, and fixed-bed column operation."

According to the news editors, the research concluded: "These results demonstrate that Fe-N/CNT is a promising adsorbent for practical dye wastewater treatment."

This research has been peer-reviewed.

For more information on this research see: N Modified Uniform Fe0 Nanoparticles Within Cnt for Efficient Removal of Methylene Blue From Wastewater. Materials Chemistry and Physics , 2026;367. Materials Chemistry and Physics can be contacted at: Elsevier Science Sa, PO Box 564, 1001 Lausanne, Switzerland. (Elsevier - www.elsevier.com ; Materials Chemistry and Physics - http://www.journals.elsevier.com/materials-chemistry-and-physics/ )

The news correspondents report that additional information may be obtained from Shuang Li, Northwest University, School of Chemical Engineering, Xian 710069, Shaanxi, People's Republic of China. Additional authors for this research include He Qu, Xuedong Ma, Dongzheng Wang, Quanyu Shi, Like Fu and Hongfei Xiao.

The direct object identifier (DOI) for that additional information is: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.matchemphys.2026.132966 . This DOI is a link to an online electronic document that is either free or for purchase, and can be your direct source for a journal article and its citation.

2.1 Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE:SCCO) is a leading integrated copper producer, renowned for its extensive copper mining operations and low-cost production capabilities. Core activities encompass large-scale copper mining, smelting, and refining through key assets like the Toquepala and Cuajone mines, alongside Mexico's strategic copper operations. The company excels in producing copper concentrates and cathodes, while also generating molybdenum and silver byproducts. Southern Copper sustains its competitive edge through significant copper reserves, supporting industrial copper supply and expansion projects. Emphasizing sustainability, the company adopts innovative mining practices and maintains robust supply chain management, positioning itself to leverage long-term trends in electric vehicles and base metals demand.

2.1 Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

Tue Oct 27, 2026: Southern Copper's Growth Prospects Clouded by Tia Maria Delays

Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE:SCCO) is navigating a complex landscape of robust earnings juxtaposed with project delays, particularly concerning its Tia Maria project in Peru. On the 27th of October 2026, the company reported record third-quarter revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and net earnings, enhanced by higher copper prices and strong contributions from its Mexican operations.

Despite these impressive figures, the company faces challenges due to falling copper prices and lower ore grades at its Peruvian mines. Southern Copper's production from its Toquepala and Cuajone mines has reportedly declined, necessitating increased output from its Mexican operations to maintain overall production levels. The delays at Tia Maria, where construction has been postponed to accommodate additional engineering work, add another layer of complexity to the company's growth outlook.

Southern Copper's successful quarter was largely driven by price increases rather than volume growth, raising concerns about the sustainability of such earnings in the face of fluctuating commodity prices. Management emphasized that while Mexican operations provided a necessary buffer, the ongoing issues in Peru must be addressed to ensure long-term stability. The company has a diverse asset base, operating across Mexico and Peru, but the current focus remains on overcoming the challenges posed by its Peruvian projects.

Looking ahead, the company has ambitious plans for growth, including a decade-long capital program aimed at increasing annual copper output. Projects like El Pilar in Mexico are set to advance, but uncertainties surrounding community relations, regulatory approvals, and production execution in Peru remain critical to Southern Copper's future performance. The market eagerly awaits updates on these initiatives, particularly the long-stalled Tia Maria project, which holds significant potential for enhancing the company's production capacity once operational.

Investors are advised to monitor Southern Copper's performance closely, as the interplay between copper prices, production volumes, and project timelines will play a pivotal role in shaping the company's trajectory. Record earnings provide a strong foundation, but the ability to manage the challenges posed by project delays and fluctuating market conditions will ultimately determine Southern Copper's growth and sustainability.

Mon Oct 26, 2026: Southern Copper Corporation Considers $968 Million Cuajone Expansion

Southern Copper Corporation is contemplating a significant expansion of its Cuajone copper mine in southern Peru, with a proposed investment of $968 million. The company announced on 28th October 2026 that the expansion would aim to increase milling capacity by 33%, from the current 90,000 tonnes per day to 120,000 tonnes per day.

Southern Copper's expansion plans would necessitate additional mining equipment and the establishment of a new production line at the Cuajone concentrator. The company estimates that the expanded operations could yield an average of 55,000 tonnes of copper and 1,400 tonnes of molybdenum annually, bolstering its output amidst current production challenges.

In addition to the immediate $968 million expansion plan, Southern Copper is exploring a larger scale enhancement that could increase milling capacity to 150,000 tonnes per day. CEO Raul Jacob indicated that while both options are under consideration, the 120,000-tonne-per-day scenario is currently deemed more feasible. A decision regarding the expansion's scale is expected in early 2027.

Despite these ambitious plans, Southern Copper has yet to finalize an investment decision or outline a specific construction timetable. The proposal comes at a time when the company faces challenges related to lower ore grades affecting its Peruvian operations, with mined copper production declining by 2.9% to 693,602 tonnes during the first nine months of 2026, primarily due to diminished grades at its mines in the region.

Cuajone serves as an open-pit copper and molybdenum operation located in Peru's Moquegua region. Southern Copper Corporation, which operates several mines and metallurgical facilities in both Peru and Mexico, is primarily owned by Grupo México, holding an 88.9% stake in the company.

Tue Oct 27, 2026: Southern Copper's Growth Prospects Clouded by Tia Maria Delays

Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE:SCCO) is navigating a complex landscape of robust earnings juxtaposed with project delays, particularly concerning its Tia Maria project in Peru. On the 27th of October 2026, the company reported record third-quarter revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and net earnings, enhanced by higher copper prices and strong contributions from its Mexican operations.

Despite these impressive figures, the company faces challenges due to falling copper prices and lower ore grades at its Peruvian mines. Southern Copper's production from its Toquepala and Cuajone mines has reportedly declined, necessitating increased output from its Mexican operations to maintain overall production levels. The delays at Tia Maria, where construction has been postponed to accommodate additional engineering work, add another layer of complexity to the company's growth outlook.

Southern Copper's successful quarter was largely driven by price increases rather than volume growth, raising concerns about the sustainability of such earnings in the face of fluctuating commodity prices. Management emphasized that while Mexican operations provided a necessary buffer, the ongoing issues in Peru must be addressed to ensure long-term stability. The company has a diverse asset base, operating across Mexico and Peru, but the current focus remains on overcoming the challenges posed by its Peruvian projects.

Looking ahead, the company has ambitious plans for growth, including a decade-long capital program aimed at increasing annual copper output. Projects like El Pilar in Mexico are set to advance, but uncertainties surrounding community relations, regulatory approvals, and production execution in Peru remain critical to Southern Copper's future performance. The market eagerly awaits updates on these initiatives, particularly the long-stalled Tia Maria project, which holds significant potential for enhancing the company's production capacity once operational.

Investors are advised to monitor Southern Copper's performance closely, as the interplay between copper prices, production volumes, and project timelines will play a pivotal role in shaping the company's trajectory. Record earnings provide a strong foundation, but the ability to manage the challenges posed by project delays and fluctuating market conditions will ultimately determine Southern Copper's growth and sustainability.

Recent News 2 of 3, Source: HourlyBusinessNews, 269 words

Mon Oct 26, 2026: Southern Copper Corporation Considers $968 Million Cuajone Expansion

Southern Copper Corporation is contemplating a significant expansion of its Cuajone copper mine in southern Peru, with a proposed investment of $968 million. The company announced on 28th October 2026 that the expansion would aim to increase milling capacity by 33%, from the current 90,000 tonnes per day to 120,000 tonnes per day.

Southern Copper's expansion plans would necessitate additional mining equipment and the establishment of a new production line at the Cuajone concentrator. The company estimates that the expanded operations could yield an average of 55,000 tonnes of copper and 1,400 tonnes of molybdenum annually, bolstering its output amidst current production challenges.

In addition to the immediate $968 million expansion plan, Southern Copper is exploring a larger scale enhancement that could increase milling capacity to 150,000 tonnes per day. CEO Raul Jacob indicated that while both options are under consideration, the 120,000-tonne-per-day scenario is currently deemed more feasible. A decision regarding the expansion's scale is expected in early 2027.

Despite these ambitious plans, Southern Copper has yet to finalize an investment decision or outline a specific construction timetable. The proposal comes at a time when the company faces challenges related to lower ore grades affecting its Peruvian operations, with mined copper production declining by 2.9% to 693,602 tonnes during the first nine months of 2026, primarily due to diminished grades at its mines in the region.

Cuajone serves as an open-pit copper and molybdenum operation located in Peru's Moquegua region. Southern Copper Corporation, which operates several mines and metallurgical facilities in both Peru and Mexico, is primarily owned by Grupo México, holding an 88.9% stake in the company.

Southern Copper Corporation has reported record third-quarter sales and net income, reflecting robust operational performance and market demand for its products. Its product portfolio includes disposable diapers and training pants, baby wipes, feminine care products, adult incontinence products, facial and bathroom tissue, paper towels, napkins, and related household goods.

Dec 04, 2025: ASUR Calls for a Shareholders' Meeting

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V.(NYSE: ASR; BMV: ASUR) (ASUR), a leading international airport group with operations in Mexico, the United States, and Colombia, today announced the call to assembly for its General Ordinary Shareholders' Meeting which will be held on January 26 th, 2026 and announced the agenda for the meeting. The following is the complete text of the call to assembly for the shareholders' meeting: CALL TO ASSEMBLY FOR ORDINARY ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING OF THE SHAREHOLDERS OF GRUPO AEROPORTUARIO DEL SURESTE, S.A.B. DE C.V. By resolution of the Board of Directors adopted at the meeting held on the September 30th 2025 and pursuant to the provisions of Articles 36, 37 and other provisions of the bylaws of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (the "Company") and Articles 181 and 183 of the General Corporations Law ("Ley General de Sociedades Mercantiles"), the Company's shareholders are hereby called to attend the Ordinary General Shareholders' Meeting (the "Meeting"), which will take place at 10 o'clock a.m. on the 26 th of January 2026, at the Company's offices at Bosque de Alisos No. 47-A 4 th floor, Colonia Bosque de las Lomas, 05120, Mexico City, Mexico, in order to discuss the following matters: A G E N D A I. Presentation, discussion and, if applicable, approval for the Company to acquire all or part of the shares and/or airport operators, including Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes, either directly or through its subsidiaries and/or special purpose vehicles. Resolutions thereon. II. Presentation, discussion and, if applicable, approval for the Company to, directly or indirectly, contract any type of debt, either through bank loans, securities issuances, or any other form of financing, and to enter into the contracts and agreements necessary and/or convenient to implement the foregoing.

Press Release article 3 of 5, Source: WEC, 313 words

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.

Press Release article 4 of 5, Source: WEC, 182 words

Nov 06, 2025: ASUR Announces Total Passenger Traffic for October 2025

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE: ASR; BMV: ASUR), ASUR, a leading international airport group with operations in Mexico, the U.S. and Colombia, today announced that passenger traffic for October 2025 reached a total of 5.3 million passengers, representing an increase of 1.0% compared to October 2024. Passenger traffic increased 5.1% year-on-year in Colombia, while it presented declines of 0.2% in Mexico and 1.7% in Puerto Rico. Passenger traffic growth in Colombia was driven by increases of 14.8% in international traffic and 2.5% in domestic traffic. Mexico reported a 0.5% decrease in domestic traffic nearly offset by a 0.1% increase in international traffic. Puerto Rico reported an increase of 10.8% in international traffic more than offset by a decrease of 3.6% in domestic traffic. All figures in this statement reflect comparisons between the period from October 1 to 31, 2025 and from October 1 to 31, 2024. Figures excluded transit and general aviation passengers for Mexico and Colombia.

Source: Company Website

Dec 04, 2025: ASUR Calls for a Shareholders' Meeting

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V.(NYSE: ASR; BMV: ASUR) (ASUR), a leading international airport group with operations in Mexico, the United States, and Colombia, today announced the call to assembly for its General Ordinary Shareholders' Meeting which will be held on January 26 th, 2026 and announced the agenda for the meeting. The following is the complete text of the call to assembly for the shareholders' meeting: CALL TO ASSEMBLY FOR ORDINARY ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING OF THE SHAREHOLDERS OF GRUPO AEROPORTUARIO DEL SURESTE, S.A.B. DE C.V. By resolution of the Board of Directors adopted at the meeting held on the September 30th 2025 and pursuant to the provisions of Articles 36, 37 and other provisions of the bylaws of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (the "Company") and Articles 181 and 183 of the General Corporations Law ("Ley General de Sociedades Mercantiles"), the Company's shareholders are hereby called to attend the Ordinary General Shareholders' Meeting (the "Meeting"), which will take place at 10 o'clock a.m. on the 26 th of January 2026, at the Company's offices at Bosque de Alisos No. 47-A 4 th floor, Colonia Bosque de las Lomas, 05120, Mexico City, Mexico, in order to discuss the following matters: A G E N D A I. Presentation, discussion and, if applicable, approval for the Company to acquire all or part of the shares and/or airport operators, including Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes, either directly or through its subsidiaries and/or special purpose vehicles. Resolutions thereon. II. Presentation, discussion and, if applicable, approval for the Company to, directly or indirectly, contract any type of debt, either through bank loans, securities issuances, or any other form of financing, and to enter into the contracts and agreements necessary and/or convenient to implement the foregoing.

Press Release article 3 of 5, Source: WEC, 313 words

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.

Press Release article 4 of 5, Source: WEC, 182 words

Nov 06, 2025: ASUR Announces Total Passenger Traffic for October 2025

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE: ASR; BMV: ASUR), ASUR, a leading international airport group with operations in Mexico, the U.S. and Colombia, today announced that passenger traffic for October 2025 reached a total of 5.3 million passengers, representing an increase of 1.0% compared to October 2024. Passenger traffic increased 5.1% year-on-year in Colombia, while it presented declines of 0.2% in Mexico and 1.7% in Puerto Rico. Passenger traffic growth in Colombia was driven by increases of 14.8% in international traffic and 2.5% in domestic traffic. Mexico reported a 0.5% decrease in domestic traffic nearly offset by a 0.1% increase in international traffic. Puerto Rico reported an increase of 10.8% in international traffic more than offset by a decrease of 3.6% in domestic traffic. All figures in this statement reflect comparisons between the period from October 1 to 31, 2025 and from October 1 to 31, 2024. Figures excluded transit and general aviation passengers for Mexico and Colombia.

Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. (ASUR) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a portfolio of 10 airports in the southeastern region, including the high-traffic Cancun International Airport. Its core business involves the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, commercial concessions, and ancillary services like retail and parking. ASUR focuses on enhancing efficiency and passenger experience to support growing aviation demand. The company's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, fueled by tourism in destinations such as Cancun and the Riviera Maya, as well as non-aeronautical revenues from expanded retail and food services, which have seen robust increases due to rising traveler spending and airport expansions. This strategic emphasis has solidified ASUR's role in Mexico's aviation industry, contributing to economic connectivity and regional development. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 11th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Activities

Fomento Económico Mexicana S.A.B. de C.V. (FEMSA), a Monterrey, Mexico-based multinational conglomerate, is primarily engaged in the production, bottling, and distribution of beverages through its Coca-Cola FEMSA subsidiary, which operates as one of the world's largest Coca-Cola franchisees. The company also manages a vast retail network, including the OXXO convenience store chain, which dominates Mexico's retail landscape and extends into select international markets. Additionally, FEMSA operates in logistics, fuel retailing, and health sciences. The fastest-growing segments include retail, driven by the aggressive expansion of OXXO stores and digital initiatives that enhance customer convenience, as well as beverage operations in emerging markets, fueled by rising consumer demand for non-alcoholic drinks and strategic acquisitions. This diversified approach has positioned FEMSA as a resilient player in the global consumer goods sector, emphasizing innovation and sustainability. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 5th largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

8.1 Activities

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V., is a leading beverage company and the largest franchise bottler for The Coca-Cola Company in Latin America, headquartered in Mexico. Its core business revolves around the production, distribution, and marketing of a diverse portfolio of non-alcoholic beverages, including sparkling drinks, bottled water, juices, teas, and energy drinks, primarily under the Coca-Cola brand. The company operates in key markets such as Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, and Guatemala, utilizing an extensive supply chain and distribution network to reach consumers efficiently. Among its fastest-growing segments are still beverages, particularly flavored waters and ready-to-drink teas, fueled by rising demand for healthier and functional options amid shifting consumer preferences. This growth is supported by strategic investments in innovation, sustainability, and digital platforms, positioning Coca-Cola FEMSA as a resilient player in the competitive beverage industry. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 13th largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

8.1 Activities

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V., is a leading beverage company and the largest franchise bottler for The Coca-Cola Company in Latin America, headquartered in Mexico. Its core business revolves around the production, distribution, and marketing of a diverse portfolio of non-alcoholic beverages, including sparkling drinks, bottled water, juices, teas, and energy drinks, primarily under the Coca-Cola brand. The company operates in key markets such as Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, and Guatemala, utilizing an extensive supply chain and distribution network to reach consumers efficiently. Among its fastest-growing segments are still beverages, particularly flavored waters and ready-to-drink teas, fueled by rising demand for healthier and functional options amid shifting consumer preferences. This growth is supported by strategic investments in innovation, sustainability, and digital platforms, positioning Coca-Cola FEMSA as a resilient player in the competitive beverage industry. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 13th largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

SECTION 8 CORPORATE PROFILE

8.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 12th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

SECTION 8 CORPORATE PROFILE

8.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 12th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

CIUDAD DE MÉXICO, 3 nov (Reuters) - La bolsa mexicana subía el martes, al reanudar operaciones tras un feriado local, mientras los inversores se mantenían atentos a las elecciones legislativas de Estados Unidos, que definirán el control del Congreso.

El índice líder S&P/BMV IPC .MXX, que agrupa a las acciones más negociadas del mercado local, ganaba un 0.84% a 70,367.51 puntos poco después de la apertura.

Los títulos de la aerolínea Volaris VOLARA.MX encabezaban las ganancias, con un salto del 8.71%. Les seguían las acciones de los grupos aeroportuarios Asur ASURB.MX, GAP GAPB.MX y Oma OMAB.MX, con alzas de un 3.00%, un 2.79% y un 2.48%, respectivamente.

Grupo Financiero Banorte reportará sus resultados trimestrales fuera de calendario tras el cierre del mercado.

(Reporte de Noé Torres)

Megacable , led by Enrique Yamuni, does not rule out modifying its mobile phone strategy to attract more users to Altán Redes as Televisa moves forward with its plans to acquire AT&T in Mexico.

During a call with analysts, Raymundo Fernández , an executive at Megacable, explained that the majority of its 845,000 mobile lines currently operate on Altán's infrastructure, while another portion uses AT&T's network.

The company could transfer more customers to Altán in 2027 and is even considering the possibility of migrating all its users to Altán Redes or establishing agreements with a third operator. For now, Megacable aims to maintain its commercial relationship with AT&T, although it acknowledges that the new scenario could lead to adjustments in the coming months.

Interestingly, Megacable also does not rule out taking advantage of sector consolidation for acquisitions and is exploring various options, from strengthening its fixed telecommunications business to repurchasing shares or increasing dividends, though it does not yet have a concrete operation to announce.

In the meantime, mobile telephony will remain a complementary business for Megacable, which does not plan to make significant investments in that segment. Its priority will be to leverage the fixed infrastructure it has built over the past years, as it defines the role that Altán Redes will play in its growth strategy.

Additionally, the company is making adjustments to its workforce. Megacable reduced more than 2,600 jobs compared to the close of 2025 and finished September with approximately 31,700 employees. This measure is part of a strategy to control costs and improve productivity, which also includes automation and artificial intelligence.

Discussion of the Federal Expenditure Budget Begins

The Chamber of Deputies is set to discuss this week the Federal Expenditure Budget for 2027 amid negotiations between agencies and institutions seeking increased resources.

The proposal includes spending exceeding 10 trillion pesos , of which around one trillion would be allocated to social programs. Legislators have until November 15 to approve it, although negotiations are anticipated to modify the distribution of resources.

One notable point is the budget for the National Electoral Institute (INE) , which has been allocated 42,274.5 million pesos in a year when it will have to organize one of the largest electoral processes in its history.

It remains to be seen whether the resignation of Guadalupe Taddei Zavala from the presidency of the organization will have any impact on negotiations, especially after previous processes where legislators did not authorize the full amount requested by the INE.

For now, days of negotiations are expected in San Lázaro , although it is unclear how much the deputies will alter the Treasury's proposal.

OECD Holds Meeting with the SHCP

The week began actively in the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit (SHCP) , following a meeting yesterday between Aida Caldera, head of the National Studies Division at the OECD , and María del Carmen Bonilla, Undersecretary of Finance .

The meeting focused on two topics of interest for the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development : understanding the federal government's plans for sustainable financing in a more challenging environment due to high international interest rates, and assessing public debt indicators.

Caldera highlighted that Mexico offers valuable insights for other emerging economies, thanks to its efforts to incorporate sustainability criteria into public finances and debt management, through the issuance of sovereign bonds aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

For her part, Bonilla explained that Mexico has been working with multilateral organizations such as the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) and the World Bank to secure financing for projects of the current administration, including the Mexico Plan.

The undersecretary assured that the federal budget is fully aligned with the SDGs, contributing to the development of a sustainable debt market. Since 2020, the issuance of thematic instruments in the Mexican market has exceeded 91 billion dollars.

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V., is a leading beverage company and the largest franchise bottler for The Coca-Cola Company in Latin America, headquartered in Mexico. Its core business revolves around the production, distribution, and marketing of a diverse portfolio of non-alcoholic beverages, including sparkling drinks, bottled water, juices, teas, and energy drinks, primarily under the Coca-Cola brand. The company operates in key markets such as Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, and Guatemala, utilizing an extensive supply chain and distribution network to reach consumers efficiently. This growth is supported by strategic investments in innovation, sustainability, and digital platforms, positioning Coca-Cola FEMSA as a resilient player in the competitive beverage industry. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 13th largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 12th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

5.1 Activities

Promotora Y Operadora De Infraestructura, S.A.B. De C.V. (PINFRA), a leading Mexican infrastructure company listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange, specializes in the development, construction, operation, and maintenance of transportation and infrastructure assets. Its core activities encompass toll roads, bridges, airports, and railways, primarily through public-private concessions that generate revenue via user fees and long-term contracts. The company plays a vital role in Mexico's economic growth by enhancing connectivity and mobility across key regions. Among its fastest-growing segments are airport operations, which have expanded significantly due to increasing passenger traffic and new terminal developments, as well as concessions for modern toll highways that benefit from rising vehicular demand and government infrastructure initiatives. PINFRA's strategic focus on sustainable projects and operational efficiency has positioned it as a key player in the sector, contributing to national development while delivering consistent returns for shareholders. It is Mexico's 3rd largest Engineering & construction company by market capitalization.

Its core business activities encompass the management of toll road concessions, airport operations, and railway systems, primarily in Mexico, with a focus on enhancing connectivity and efficiency in transportation networks. The company has diversified into complementary areas such as industrial and urban infrastructure projects, leveraging public-private partnerships to drive growth. Among its fastest-growing segments are toll road concessions, fueled by increasing vehicular traffic and strategic expansions, as well as airport operations, which have benefited from rising passenger volumes and modernization efforts. PINFRA's commitment to sustainable practices and operational excellence positions it as a key player in Mexico's infrastructure sector, supporting economic development through reliable and innovative solutions. Director

Megacable will maintain its business relationship with AT&T Mexico, even with the acquisition of this company by Grupo Televisa, one of its main competitors in fixed networks. However, Megacable indicated that it could transfer all mobile customers currently served through AT&T to Altán Redes, without altering its business strategy.

The company, which currently has 844,841 mobile subscribers, believes that this business will continue as a complement to its Internet and pay-TV services, without the need for additional investment in cellular infrastructure, company executives stated during a conference call with analysts regarding the third-quarter results of 2026.

"We would like to maintain the relationship with AT&T if they wish to continue, but we have no issue moving all our subscribers to the Altán platform if needed," said Raymundo Fernández, Deputy General Director of Megacable.

Currently, the majority of Megacable's mobile users receive service through the infrastructure of Altán Redes, operator of the Shared Network, while a minority utilizes the AT&T Mexico network.

The acquisition of AT&T by Televisa introduces a new variable in that wholesale relationship, as Megacable and Izzi, a subsidiary of Televisa, compete directly for broadband and pay-TV customers in various cities across the country.

However, the acquisition still must complete its closing process, which is expected in the first quarter of 2027. Megacable executives did not announce the termination of their agreement with AT&T nor anticipatory decisions from Televisa regarding the continuation of the wholesale service.

Telcel was already in Megacable's plans

The possibility of diversifying mobile providers did not arise with the announcement of AT&T's acquisition.

El Economista reported on May 8 that Megacable was seeking a strategic alliance with Telcel, operator of América Móvil, to enhance its mobile offering and complement the services it already received from AT&T and Altán Redes.

"In mobile, we have the best service from two companies. One is AT&T, and the other is Altán. We are looking at how to integrate more players, like Telcel, in the future," Fernández told El Economista at that time.

The intention was to leverage Telcel's coverage to expand Megacable's commercial possibilities and offer mobile connectivity in more areas of the country, particularly where the infrastructure of its current providers showed limitations.

At that time, Megacable had 740,354 mobile subscribers.

The reported base now stands at 844,841 users, a difference of 104,487 lines, equivalent to a 14.1% growth compared to the figure released in May.

The fixed business will continue to concentrate investments

Fernández insisted that Megacable does not intend to divert resources from its primary activity to build a mobile operation with its own infrastructure.

"Mobile service is a complement for our subscribers; it does not require Capex, goes directly to our network, and contributes to the company," he explained.

"We are focusing on what we told you before and we are not wasting any strategic effort of our company on convergence issues," the executive added.

This stance confirms that mobile telephony will continue to function as a commercial tool to strengthen relationships with customers of fixed services, rather than becoming a new capital-intensive activity.

This position aligns with Megacable's shift in financial priorities after five years of infrastructure expansion.

At the close of the third quarter of 2026, the company reported 19.91 million homes covered and 6.08 million Internet subscribers, while its network reached a length of 111,855 kilometers.

Megacable, un operador de telecomunicaciones mexicano, mantendrá su estrategia de maximizar el valor de su negocio, centrada principalmente en servicios de línea fija, tras la adquisición del negocio móvil de AT&T en México por parte de su competidor Grupo Televisa. La empresa continuará ofreciendo servicios como operador móvil virtual y no anticipa inversiones relacionadas con la adquisición de Televisa, el segundo operador móvil más grande del país. Megacable cuenta actualmente con 844,841 suscriptores a su servicio móvil, que opera principalmente utilizando la infraestructura de Altán Redes, con una menor porción en la infraestructura de AT&T. Por otro lado, Mercado Libre, la plataforma de comercio electrónico latinoamericana, inauguró su primer centro logístico en Tezontepec, Hidalgo, que incorpora robots para la preparación y procesamiento de pedidos. Esta instalación, parte de una inversión acumulativa de $604 millones en Hidalgo, comenzará operaciones con 240 robots y se espera que alcance hasta 1,000 a plena capacidad. La expansión de Mercado Libre en Hidalgo forma parte de una inversión anunciada de más de $4.6 mil millones para México hasta 2026.

La instalación, que forma parte de una inversión acumulada de 604 millones de dólares en Hidalgo, comenzará a operar con 240 robots y llegará a 1,000 cuando opere a su máxima capacidad.

La expansión de Mercado Libre en Hidalgo estaba contemplada en la inversión de más de 4,600 millones de dólares que la empresa anunció para México en 2026.

Las acciones de Intel, fabricante estadounidense de chips y semiconductores, registraron su mayor caída diaria desde 1974, luego de que la compañía anticipó ingresos y ganancias inferiores a las esperadas para el cuarto trimestre, ante la persistente debilidad del mercado de computadoras personales.

Intel perdió 29%, su peor desempeño bursátil en más de cinco décadas. Los títulos cerraron en 65.76 dólares, su nivel más bajo desde abril.

Intel prevé ingresos de entre 15,000 y 16,000 millones de dólares para el último trimestre del año, por debajo de los aproximadamente 17,000 millones que esperaban los analistas.

Alaska Air Group anunció que recortará unos 200 puestos de trabajo no contractuales, ya que el aumento vertiginoso de los precios del combustible y los desafíos geopolíticos están afectando sus finanzas, y su director ejecutivo advirtió sobre una posible pérdida anual de 700 millones de dólares.

Estos recortes sugieren que la crisis de los precios del combustible vinculada a la guerra con Irán —que ya ha llevado a las aerolíneas estadounidenses a aumentar las tarifas y frenar el crecimiento de los vuelos— ahora está afectando los empleos en la industria aérea.

También ponen de relieve la creciente presión financiera sobre Alaska Air, que persigue una ambiciosa expansión en el sector de los viajes internacionales y de primera clase, con un fuerte crecimiento de los ingresos que lucha por compensar el aumento de los costos del combustible.

Servicios Adicionales del Auditor Externo Aprobados por el Comite de Auditoria

FECHA: 30/10/2026

BOLSA MEXICANA DE VALORES, S.A.B. DE C.V., INFORMA:

CLAVE COTIZACIÓN :

GISSA

RAZÓN SOCIAL :

GRUPO INDUSTRIAL SALTILLO, S.A.B. DE C.V.

RAZÓN SOCIAL DEL AUDITOR EXTERNO :

Galaz, Yamazaki, Ruiz Urquiza, S.C.

DESCRIPCIÓN DE LOS SERVICIOS ADICIONALES APROBADOS POR EL COMITÉ DE AUDITORIA :

AVISO DE LA CONTRATACIÓN DE SERVICIOS ADICIONALES A LOS DE AUDITORIA

Grupo Industrial Saltillo, S.A.B. de C.V. (en lo sucesivo la "Sociedad" o la "Emisora") informa a esa Comisión Nacional Bancaria y de Valores la contratación de servicios adicionales a los servicios de auditoría del Auditor Externo del Despacho Galaz, Yamazaki, Ruiz Urquiza, S.C. (Deloitte) en el que presta sus servicios dicho Auditor Externo (el "Auditor"), consistente en:

  • Elaboración de dictamen del Seguro Social, INFONAVIT y Contribuciones locales, por un monto aproximado de honorarios de $700,000 M.N.

  • Asesoría fiscal en materia de precios de transferencia y Dictamen Fiscal, por un costo aproximado de $3,300,000 M.N.

  • Elaboración de estudio respecto del Estado de Información No Financiera de las empresas de Draxton Global a fin de dar cumplimiento a la normativa correspondiente. El servicio tiene un costo aproximado de $800,000 M.N.

La contratación de los servicios adicionales antes mencionados, fueron autorizados por el Comité de Auditoría el 16 de octubre de 2026 y por el Consejo de Administración de la Sociedad el 20 de octubre de 2026. Dichos servicios equivalen a un monto total de $4,800,000 M.N. contrastado con los honorarios por la auditoría externa de estados financieros básicos anuales que corresponden a un monto total de $18,000,000 M.N. aproximadamente.

La prestación de los servicios adicionales descritos en el presente aviso no afecta la independencia del Auditor, ni del equipo de trabajo de auditores externos, en la prestación a la Sociedad del servicio de auditoría de estados financieros básicos del ejercicio en curso, en virtud de que los servicios adicionales: (i) no se ubican en la lista establecida en el Artículo 6, fracción VII de las Disposiciones de Carácter General Aplicables a las Entidades y Emisoras Supervisadas por la Comisión Nacional Bancaria y de Valores que Contraten Servicios de Auditoría Externa de Estados Financiero Básicos (las "Disposiciones"); (ii) el Auditor y el respectivo equipo de trabajo, no estarán en la posición de auditar su propio trabajo; (iii) no actuarán como parte de la administración o del personal de la Sociedad, ni realizarán actividades cuya responsabilidad recaiga en la administración o el personal de la Sociedad; y (iv) dichos servicios no pondrán al Auditor en la posición de defensor o abogado de la Sociedad y la prestación de los servicios no representará un conflicto de interés entre el Auditor y la Sociedad.

Informamos lo anterior de acuerdo con lo previsto en el artículo 19 de las Disposiciones. Atentamente,

Grupo Industrial Saltillo, S.A.B. de C.V.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

Monterrey, México, 30 de octubre 2026 - Arca Continental, S.A.B. de C.V. (BMV: AC*) ("Arca Continental" o "AC"), el segundo embotellador más grande de Coca-Cola en América Latina, anunció sus resultados para el tercer trimestre de 2026 y acumulado a septiembre 2026 ("3T26" y "9M26").

DATOS RELEVANTES PARA EL TERCER TRIMESTRE DE 2026

  • Ventas Netas incrementaron 5.9% en comparación con el 3T25, registrando Ps. 66,613 millones.

  • EBITDA aumentó 6.2% a Ps. 13,625 millones con un margen de 20.5%.

  • Utilidad Neta fue de Ps. 5,054 millones con un margen de 7.6%.

DATOS RELEVANTES PARA EL ACUMULADO A SEPTIEMBRE 2026

  • Ventas Netas incrementaron 2.1% en comparación con el 9M25, registrando Ps. 187,229 millones.

  • EBITDA aumentó 2.1% comparado con el mismo periodo de 2025 a Ps. 37,388 millones con un margen de 20.0%.

  • Utilidad Neta fue de Ps. 13,798 millones con un margen de 7.4%.

COMENTARIO DEL DIRECTOR GENERAL

"Durante el tercer trimestre de 2026 logramos una mejora significativa en el desempeño de nuestras operaciones, con crecimiento de 4.6% en volumen consolidado y de 6.2% en EBITDA, alcanzando un margen de 20.5%. Estos resultados reflejan la capacidad de nuestro modelo de negocio para adaptarse con velocidad y flexibilidad a las condiciones de cada mercado, fortaleciendo la ejecución comercial y operativa, al tiempo que mantenemos una gestión financiera prudente", señaló Arturo Gutiérrez, Director General de Arca Continental.

"Seguiremos enfocados en fortalecer nuestras capacidades comerciales y digitales, mantenernos cerca de clientes y consumidores y ejecutar con disciplina en cada uno de nuestros mercados, con una visión de largo plazo orientada a generar valor sostenible y contribuir al desarrollo de las comunidades donde operamos", agregó.

Acerca de Arca Continental

Arca Continental es una empresa dedicada a la producción, distribución y venta de bebidas de las marcas propiedad de The Coca-Cola Company, así como de botanas bajo las marcas Bokados en México, Inalecsa en Ecuador, y Wise en los Estados Unidos de América. Con una destacada trayectoria de más de 100 años, Arca Continental es el segundo embotellador de Coca-Cola más grande de América Latina y uno de las más importantes del mundo. En su franquicia de Coca-Cola, la empresa atiende a una población de más de 130 millones en la región norte y occidente de México, así como en Ecuador, Perú, en la región norte de Argentina y en la región suroeste de Estados Unidos. Arca Continental cotiza en la Bolsa Mexicana de Valores bajo el símbolo "AC".

Para más información sobre Arca Continental, favor de visitarwww.arcacontal.com

Contacto con medios:saladeprensa@arcacontal.com

Monterrey, Mexico, October 30, 2026 -Arca Continental, S.A.B. de C.V. (BMV: AC*) ("Arca Continental" or "AC"), the second-largest Coca-Cola bottler in Latin America, announced its results for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 ("3Q26" and "9M26").


THIRD QUARTER 2026 HIGHLIGHTS

  • Net sales increased 5.9% when compared to 3Q25, totaling Ps. 66,613 million.

  • EBITDA grew 6.2% to Ps. 13,625 million with a margin of 20.5%.

  • Net Income reached Ps. 5,054 million with a margin of 7.6%.

FIRST NINE MONTHS 2026 HIGHLIGHTS

  • Net Sales increased 2.1% when compared to 9M25, totaling Ps. 187,229 million.

  • EBITDA grew 2.1% when compared to 9M25, at Ps. 37,388 million with a margin of 20.0%.

  • Net Income reached Ps. 13,798 million with a margin of 7.4%.



COMMENTS FROM THE CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER

"During the third quarter of 2026 we achieved a significant improvement in the performance of our operations, with 4.6% growth in consolidated volume and a 6.2% increase in EBITDA, reaching a margin of 20.5%. These results reflect the capability of our business model to adapt rapidly and with flexibility to the conditions of each market, strengthening our commercial and operational execution, while maintaining prudent financial management", stated Arturo Gutierrez, Chief Executive Officer of Arca Continental.

"We will continue to focus on making our commercial and digital capabilities stronger, remain close to our customers and consumers, and execute with discipline in every one of our markets, with a long-term vision aimed at generating sustainable value and contributing to the development of the communities we serve", he added.




About Arca Continental

Arca Continental is a company engaged in the production, distribution, and sale of beverages under The Coca-Cola Company's brands, as well as savory snacks under the Bokados brand in Mexico, Inalecsa in Ecuador, and Wise in the United States. With a distinguished track record of over 100 years, Arca Continental is the second-largest Coca-Cola bottler in the Americas and one of the most important in the world. Through its Coca-Cola franchise, the company serves a population of over 130 million across northern and western Mexico, Ecuador, Peru, northern Argentina, and the southwestern United States. Arca Continental is publicly traded on the Mexican Stock Exchange under the symbol "AC".

For more information about Arca Continental, please visitwww.arcacontal.com

Media contact:saladeprensa@arcacontal.com

SECTION 1: BIOGRAPHY: RAUL REVUELTA MUSALEM, CEO

Bachelor of Economics from the Instituto Tecnologico de Estudios Superiores de Monterrey, was appointed CEO of Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico (GAP) in April 2018. He has 20 years of experience in the airport and infrastructure sector.

Between 2005 and 2015, he held various positions at GAP, including Director of Administration and Finance (CFO) and Chief Commercial Officer (CCO). One of his major achievements was leading the monumental project known as the "Cross Border Xpress," the only bi-national bridge in the world connecting Mexico and the United States, which has brought countless benefits to both nations.

Previously, he served as Deputy Director of Finance at the Secretaria de Comunicaciones y Transportes (SCT) for six years, where he participated in various privatization processes in the sector and gained extensive knowledge in the field of federal concessions.

He was recently appointed Vice President of the International Council of Airports for Latin America and the Caribbean (ACI-LAC) for the 2024-2025 term, an organization that operates in 41 countries and represents more than 350 air terminals in Latin America and the Caribbean.

SECTION 1: BIOGRAPHY: RAUL REVUELTA MUSALEM, CEO

Bachelor of Economics from the Instituto Tecnologico de Estudios Superiores de Monterrey, was appointed CEO of Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico (GAP) in April 2018. He has 20 years of experience in the airport and infrastructure sector.

Between 2005 and 2015, he held various positions at GAP, including Director of Administration and Finance (CFO) and Chief Commercial Officer (CCO). One of his major achievements was leading the monumental project known as the "Cross Border Xpress," the only bi-national bridge in the world connecting Mexico and the United States, which has brought countless benefits to both nations.

Previously, he served as Deputy Director of Finance at the Secretaria de Comunicaciones y Transportes (SCT) for six years, where he participated in various privatization processes in the sector and gained extensive knowledge in the field of federal concessions.

He was recently appointed Vice President of the International Council of Airports for Latin America and the Caribbean (ACI-LAC) for the 2024-2025 term, an organization that operates in 41 countries and represents more than 350 air terminals in Latin America and the Caribbean.
